# STEP 2: DATA IMPORT & BASELINE VERIFICATION

```{r data_import}
# HouseholdID is an 18-digit ID. Import as character to prevent numeric rounding.
hh_char <- c(HouseholdID = "character")
d01 <- read.csv("data/raw/D01_Population_Profile.csv", colClasses = hh_char)
d02 <- read.csv("data/raw/D02_Learning_Profile.csv", colClasses = hh_char)
d03 <- read.csv("data/raw/D03_Economic_Participation.csv", colClasses = hh_char)
d11 <- read.csv("data/raw/D11_Labour_Market.csv", colClasses = hh_char)

dim_summary <- data.frame(
  Dataset = c("D01_Population", "D02_Learning", "D03_Economic", "D11_Labour"),
  Rows = c(nrow(d01), nrow(d02), nrow(d03), nrow(d11)),
  Columns = c(ncol(d01), ncol(d02), ncol(d03), ncol(d11))
)
kable(dim_summary, caption = "Baseline Raw Dataset Dimensions")


```

# DIAGNOSTIC CHECKS ACROSS ALL DATASETS

```{r diagnostics, comment=NA}
all_datasets <- list(
  D01_Population = d01,
  D02_Learning   = d02,
  D03_Economic   = d03,
  D11_Labour     = d11
)

# 1. Exact Duplicate Rows Summary
duplicate_summary <- data.frame(
  Dataset = names(all_datasets),
  Exact_Duplicate_Rows = sapply(all_datasets, function(df) sum(duplicated(df)))
)
kable(duplicate_summary, caption = "Summary of Exact Duplicate Rows Across Raw Datasets")

# 2. Missing Values Summary
missing_summary <- map_df(names(all_datasets), function(name) {
  df <- all_datasets[[name]]
  missing_vals <- colSums(is.na(df))
  missing_vals <- missing_vals[missing_vals > 0]
  
  if (length(missing_vals) > 0) {
    tibble(
      Dataset = name,
      Column = names(missing_vals),
      Missing_Count = as.integer(missing_vals),
      Missing_Pct = round(as.integer(missing_vals) / nrow(df) * 100, 2)
    )
  } else {
    tibble(Dataset = name, Column = "None", Missing_Count = 0, Missing_Pct = 0)
  }
})
kable(missing_summary, caption = "Missing Value Breakdown per Dataset")

# 3. Column Data Types Overview
col_types_summary <- map_df(names(all_datasets), function(name) {
  df <- all_datasets[[name]]
  types <- sapply(df, function(x) paste(class(x), collapse = ", "))
  
  tibble(
    Dataset = name,
    Total_Columns = ncol(df),
    Numeric_Cols = sum(types %in% c("numeric", "integer")),
    Character_Cols = sum(types == "character"),
    Factor_or_Other = sum(!types %in% c("numeric","integer", "character"))
  )
})

kable(col_types_summary, caption = "Column Data Type Distribution Across Raw Datasets")



```

# STEP 3: FUNCTIONS

```{r utility_functions}
format_ids <- function(df) {
  hh_names <- c("household_id", "HouseholdID")
  p_names  <- c("person_number", "PersonNumber")
  hh_col <- hh_names[hh_names %in% names(df)][1]
  p_col  <- p_names[p_names %in% names(df)][1]

  df %>%
    mutate(
      household_id_clean = str_trim(as.character(.data[[hh_col]])),
      person_number_clean = str_trim(as.character(.data[[p_col]])),
      composite_id = paste(household_id_clean, person_number_clean, sep = "_")
    )
}

clean_province <- function(df) {
  if ("Province" %in% names(df)) {
    df %>% mutate(province_clean = str_to_title(str_trim(as.character(Province))))
  } else if ("province" %in% names(df)) {
    df %>% mutate(province_clean = str_to_title(str_trim(as.character(province))))
  } else if ("ProvinceCode" %in% names(df)) {
    df %>% mutate(province_clean = as.character(ProvinceCode))
  } else {
    df %>% mutate(province_clean = "Unspecified")
  }
}

```

# STEP 4: BUILDING THE KEYS

```{r build_keys}
d01 <- format_ids(d01)
d02 <- format_ids(d02)
d03 <- format_ids(d03)
d11 <- format_ids(d11)

```

# STEP 5: DATA CLEANING

```{r data_cleaning}
# D01: Population Cleaning
d01_clean <- d01 %>%
  filter(!is.na(HouseholdID)) %>%
  mutate(age = as.numeric(Age)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(age), age >= 15 & age <= 64) %>%
  clean_province() %>%
  distinct(composite_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# D02: Learning Profile Cleaning
d02_clean <- d02 %>%
  mutate(
    edu_code_num = as.numeric(EducationLevelCode),
    edu_group = case_when(
      edu_code_num < 10 ~ "Primary or Lower",
      edu_code_num %in% c(10, 11, 12) ~ "Secondary / Matric",
      edu_code_num > 12 & edu_code_num < 98 ~ "Tertiary / Diploma / Degree",
      TRUE ~ "Other / Unspecified"
    ),
    EducationAttendanceCode = na_if(EducationAttendanceCode, "N/A"),
    EducationAttendanceCode = na_if(EducationAttendanceCode, "Unknown"),
    EducationAttendanceCode = na_if(EducationAttendanceCode, "not recorded")
  ) %>%
  distinct(composite_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# D03: Economic Participation Cleaning
d03_clean <- d03 %>%
  mutate(
    salary_amount_raw = as.numeric(SalaryAmountRaw),
    salary_bad = salary_amount_raw < 0 | salary_amount_raw > 1e300,
    salary_amount_raw = if_else(salary_bad, NA_real_, salary_amount_raw)
  ) %>%
  select(-salary_bad) %>%
  distinct(composite_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# D11: Labour Force Target Cleaning
d11_clean <- d11 %>%
  mutate(composite_id = paste(composite_id, SurveyYear, Quarter, sep = "_")) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ if_else(. > 1e300, NA_real_, .))) %>%
  mutate(
    emp_code_num = as.numeric(EmploymentStatusCode),
    monthly_amount_raw = if_else(MonthlyAmountRaw < 0, NA_real_, MonthlyAmountRaw),
    hours_worked_raw = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(HoursWorkedRaw)),
    hours_worked_raw = if_else(hours_worked_raw < 0 | hours_worked_raw > 1e300,
                                NA_real_, hours_worked_raw),
    status_label = case_when(
      emp_code_num == 1 ~ "Employed",
      emp_code_num == 2 ~ "Unemployed",
      emp_code_num == 3 ~ "Discouraged Seeker",
      emp_code_num == 4 ~ "Other Inactive",
      TRUE ~ "Unspecified"
    ),
    age_valid = Age >= 0 & Age <= 100
  ) %>%
  filter(age_valid) %>%
  group_by(OccupationCode) %>%
  mutate(hours_worked_raw = if_else(is.na(hours_worked_raw),
                                     median(hours_worked_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
                                     hours_worked_raw)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(hours_worked_raw = if_else(is.nan(hours_worked_raw), NA_real_,
                                     hours_worked_raw)) %>%
  distinct(composite_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

d01_clean <- d01_clean %>% select(-any_of(c("SurveyVersion", "DataCollectorID", "BatchNumber")))

```

# STEP 6: VERIFICATION CHECKS

```{r verification_checks, comment=NA}
cleaned_datasets <- list(
  D01_Clean = d01_clean,
  D02_Clean = d02_clean,
  D03_Clean = d03_clean,
  D11_Clean = d11_clean
)

# 1. Duplicate composite IDs
sapply(cleaned_datasets, function(df) sum(duplicated(df$composite_id)))

# 2. Sentinel max values (> 1e300)
sapply(cleaned_datasets, function(df) {
  num_cols <- df %>% select(where(is.numeric))
  sum(num_cols > 1e300, na.rm = TRUE)
})

# 3. Negative values in monetary/hours columns
c(
  d03_neg_salary  = sum(d03_clean$salary_amount_raw < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  d11_neg_monthly = sum(d11_clean$monthly_amount_raw < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  d11_neg_hours   = sum(d11_clean$hours_worked_raw < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)

# 4. D11 quarter balance
table(d11_clean$Quarter)

# 5. Recoding Traceability Checks
table(Raw = d02_clean$EducationLevelCode, Recoded = d02_clean$edu_group, useNA = "ifany")
table(Raw = d11_clean$EmploymentStatusCode, Recoded = d11_clean$status_label, useNA = "ifany")

# 6. Income Distribution Screening
quantile(d03_clean$salary_amount_raw, probs = c(0.5, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99, 1), na.rm = TRUE)
quantile(d11_clean$monthly_amount_raw, probs = c(0.5, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99, 1), na.rm = TRUE)

```

# STEP 7: CAN D11 BE JOINED TO D01/D02/D03?

```{r relationship_check, comment=NA}
d01_hh <- unique(d01_clean$HouseholdID)
d11_hh <- unique(d11_clean$HouseholdID)
d01_pkey <- unique(paste(d01_clean$HouseholdID, d01_clean$PersonNumber))
d11_pkey <- unique(paste(d11_clean$HouseholdID, d11_clean$PersonNumber))

rel_check <- tibble(
  Check = c("Household IDs (D01 found in D11)", "Person keys (D01 found in D11)"),
  Matched = c(sum(d01_hh %in% d11_hh), sum(d01_pkey %in% d11_pkey)),
  Total_D01 = c(length(d01_hh), length(d01_pkey))
)
kable(rel_check, caption = "D01 vs D11 key overlap")

area01 <- unique(substr(d01_hh, 1, 6))
area11 <- unique(substr(d11_hh, 1, 6))
cat("Area/cluster code overlap:", sum(area01 %in% area11), "of", length(area01), "\n")

```

Zero overlap exists at both household and person level.
**D11 cannot be row-joined to D01-D03.** We treat them as two parallel tracks: Track A (D11 alone, all 4 quarters) and Track B (D01+D02+D03 joined, Q1 2024 only).

# STEP 8: INTEGRATING D01 x D02 x D03 (TRACK B)

```{r trackb_join, comment=NA}
pkey01 <- paste(d01_clean$HouseholdID, d01_clean$PersonNumber)
pkey02 <- paste(d02_clean$HouseholdID, d02_clean$PersonNumber)
pkey03 <- paste(d03_clean$HouseholdID, d03_clean$PersonNumber)

match_evidence <- tibble(
  Check = c("D01 keys found in D02", "D01 keys found in D03"),
  Matched = c(sum(pkey01 %in% pkey02), sum(pkey01 %in% pkey03)),
  Total = length(pkey01),
  Pct = round(100 * Matched / Total, 2)
)
kable(match_evidence, caption = "D01-D02-D03 person-key match rate")

d01_clean <- d01_clean %>% mutate(pkey = paste(HouseholdID, PersonNumber))
d02_clean <- d02_clean %>% mutate(pkey = paste(HouseholdID, PersonNumber))
d03_clean <- d03_clean %>% mutate(pkey = paste(HouseholdID, PersonNumber))

n_before <- nrow(d01_clean)

d02_cols <- c("pkey", "EducationLevelCode", "EducationAttendanceCode",
              "InstitutionTypeCode", "GradeCode", "TotalEducationFees",
              "NoFeesSchoolCode", "edu_group")
d03_cols <- c("pkey", "WageWorkCode", "BusinessWorkCode", "LookingForWorkCode",
              "VolunteerWorkCode", "RetiredCode", "SectorCode", "salary_amount_raw",
              "EmploymentStatus1Code", "EmploymentStatus2Code")

household_profile <- d01_clean %>%
  inner_join(d02_clean %>% select(all_of(d02_cols)), by = "pkey") %>%
  inner_join(d03_clean %>% select(all_of(d03_cols)), by = "pkey")

n_after <- nrow(household_profile)
keys_unique <- length(unique(household_profile$pkey)) == n_after
cat("Rows before join:", n_before, " | after join:", n_after, "\n")
cat("1:1 join confirmed (no fan-out):", keys_unique, "\n")

```

# STEP 9: FEATURE ENGINEERING

```{r trackb_features, comment=NA}
# Track B (D01+D02+D03, Q1 2024)
household_profile <- household_profile %>%
  mutate(
    gender = case_when(
      SexCode == 1 ~ "Male", SexCode == 2 ~ "Female", TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    geo_type = case_when(
      GeoTypeCode == 1 ~ "Urban",
      GeoTypeCode == 2 ~ "Rural (Traditional)",
      GeoTypeCode == 3 ~ "Rural (Farms)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    population_group = case_when(
      PopulationGroupCode == 1 ~ "Black African",
      PopulationGroupCode == 2 ~ "Coloured",
      PopulationGroupCode == 3 ~ "Indian/Asian",
      PopulationGroupCode == 4 ~ "White",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    age_band = if_else(age >= 15 & age <= 34, "Youth (15-34)", "Adult (35-64)"),
    employment_status_q1 = case_when(
      EmploymentStatus1Code == 1 ~ "Employed",
      EmploymentStatus1Code == 2 ~ "Unemployed",
      EmploymentStatus1Code == 8 ~ "Not Economically Active",
      TRUE ~ "Unspecified"
    ),
    job_search_active = case_when(
      LookingForWorkCode == 1 ~ "Actively Looking",
      LookingForWorkCode == 2 ~ "Not Looking",
      TRUE ~ "Not Applicable"
    ),
    has_income = !is.na(salary_amount_raw) & salary_amount_raw > 0,
    has_salary_income = if_else(has_income, "Has Salary Income", "No Salary Income"),
    currently_studying = case_when(
      EducationAttendanceCode == "1" ~ "Yes",
      EducationAttendanceCode == "2" ~ "No",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    not_engaged = currently_studying == "No" &
      employment_status_q1 != "Employed" &
      job_search_active != "Actively Looking",
    not_engaged_flag = if_else(not_engaged, "Possibly Disengaged",
                                "Engaged/Studying/Working", missing = NA_character_)
  ) %>%
  select(-has_income, -not_engaged)

kable(as.data.frame(table(household_profile$employment_status_q1)),
      col.names = c("Q1 employment status", "N"), caption = "Track B employment status")

```

# MODELLING STRATEGY & MODEL BUILDING

## 1.1 Analytical Question & Project Scope

The primary objective of this study is to address the following analytical question:

> **"To what extent can demographic, regional, and educational indicators predict individual unemployment risk in South Africa, and which predictors hold the highest influence?"**

By framing this as a data-driven policy problem, the analysis aims to identify structural vulnerabilities within the labour market and highlight critical factors contributing to labour market exclusion.

## 1.2 Modelling Type

This problem is formulated as a **supervised binary classification** task.
The target variable, `Unemployed`, is binary: \* **`1` ("Unemployed")**: Individuals actively seeking work or classified as unemployed.
\* **`0` ("Not_Unemployed")**: Individuals who are employed, discouraged job-seekers, or otherwise inactive.

## 1.3 Target Definition & Target Leakage Prevention

To ensure valid predictive modeling and avoid data leakage, strict governance controls were applied during feature selection:

1.  **Outcome-Derived Identifiers:** Variables directly derived from the target or employment status code (such as `NEETCode`, `labour_force`, `status_label`) were dropped.
2.  **Post-Unemployment Features:** Attributes that exist exclusively for employed individuals (e.g., `MonthlyAmountRaw`, `HoursWorkedRaw`, `OccupationCode`, `IndustryCode`, `InformalEmploymentCode`) were removed. Including these would cause artificial leakage, as missingness or values in these fields perfectly separate employed individuals from unemployed ones.
3.  **Weight & Identifier Removal:** Non-predictive survey identifiers (`HouseholdID`, `PersonNumber`) and survey sampling weights (`QuarterWeight`, `AnnualWeight`) were excluded.

## 1.4 Preprocessing Strategy

Data preprocessing is managed using the `recipes` framework to ensure reproducibility and prevent train-test data contamination: \* **Factor Level Handling:** Novel categorical levels in the test set are handled via `step_novel()`, while missing categorical values are assigned an explicit `"unknown"` category using `step_unknown()`.
\* **Imputation:** Missing continuous predictor values are imputed using median imputation via `step_impute_median()` directly within the recipe pipeline prior to dummy transformation.
\* **Variance & Linear Combination Filtering:** Variables with zero or near-zero variance are removed using `step_nzv()` and `step_zv()`, while exact linear dependencies are resolved via `step_lincomb()`.
\* **Categorical Encoding:** Predictors are dynamic dummy-encoded using `step_dummy()` for model compatibility.

## 1.5 Candidate Models & Theoretical Assumptions

Three diverse algorithms were selected to balance interpretability, probability calibration, and non-linear predictive capacity:

1.  **Logistic Regression (`glm` - Baseline Model):**
    - *Rationale:* Serves as an interpretable linear baseline.
    - *Assumptions:* Assumes a linear relationship between numeric predictors and the log-odds of being unemployed, absence of severe multicollinearity, and independent observations.
2.  **Naïve Bayes (`e1071`):**
    - *Rationale:* A probabilistic classifier that efficiently processes high-dimensional, categorical baseline data.
    - *Assumptions:* Assumes class-conditional independence among predictors (i.e., predictors are independent given the target class).
3.  **Random Forest (`ranger` / `caret` - Advanced Model):**
    - *Rationale:* An ensemble of decision trees capable of capturing non-linear interactions and complex relationships without strict distribution assumptions.
    - *Assumptions:* Non-parametric; does not assume linear relationships or specific variable distributions.

## 1.6 Resampling & Tuning Design

To ensure robust evaluation and prevent overfitting: \* **Stratified Split:** Data is partitioned into a **70% Training Set** and a **30% Test Set** using stratified sampling on the `Unemployed` outcome to preserve class proportions.
\* **Cross-Validation:** Models are trained using **5-Fold Cross-Validation** (`trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5)`), ensuring parameter stability and reliable performance estimation across folds.

# STEP 11: MODELLING PREPARATION & LEAKAGE CONTROL

## 11.1 Target definition

```{r target_definition, comment=NA}
library(rsample)
library(recipes)

d11_model <- d11_clean %>%
  mutate(Unemployed = case_when(
    status_label == "Unemployed"                     ~ 1L,
    status_label %in% c("Employed", "Other Inactive",
                        "Discouraged Seeker")        ~ 0L,
    TRUE                                              ~ NA_integer_
  )) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Unemployed))

cat("Rows available for modelling:", nrow(d11_model), "\n")
cat("Class distribution (Unemployed):\n")
print(prop.table(table(d11_model$Unemployed)))

```

## 11.2 Leakage control

```{r leakage_removal, comment=NA}
identifier_vars <- c(
  "HouseholdID", "PersonNumber", "SurveyDateRaw",
  "household_id_clean", "person_number_clean",
  "composite_id", "pkey"
)

weight_vars <- c("QuarterWeight", "AnnualWeight", "PersonWeight")

outcome_derived_vars <- c(
  "EmploymentStatusCode", "emp_code_num", "status_label",
  "ExpandedEmploymentStatusCode", "UnemploymentStatusCode",
  "NEETCode", "neet", "labour_force"
)

unemployed_or_employed_only <- c(
  "OccupationCode", "IndustryCode",
  "Sector1Code", "Sector2Code",
  "InformalEmploymentCode", "informal_employment",
  "LongTermUnemploymentCode", "UnderemploymentCode",
  "MonthlyAmountRaw", "monthly_amount_raw",
  "HoursWorkedRaw", "hours_worked_raw"
)

drop_vars <- c(identifier_vars, weight_vars,
               outcome_derived_vars, unemployed_or_employed_only)

d11_model <- d11_model %>% select(-any_of(drop_vars))

```

## 11.3 Train/test split (stratified)

```{r train_test_split, comment=NA}
set.seed(2026)

split <- initial_split(d11_model, prop = 0.7, strata = Unemployed)
train <- training(split)
test  <- testing(split)

```

## 11.4 Preprocessing recipe

```{r recipe_fit, comment=NA}
rec <- recipe(Unemployed ~ ., data = train) %>%
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors())  %>%
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_nzv(all_predictors())            %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = FALSE)  %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_lincomb(all_numeric_predictors())

rec_prepped <- prep(rec, training = train)

train_baked <- bake(rec_prepped, new_data = train)
test_baked  <- bake(rec_prepped, new_data = test)

```

## 11.5 Before/after validation evidence

```{r validation_evidence, comment=NA}
validation <- tibble(
  Stage   = c("d11_clean (after cleaning)",
              "d11_model (after target + leakage drop)",
              "Train (70%)", "Test (30%)",
              "Train (baked)", "Test (baked)"),
  Rows    = c(nrow(d11_clean), nrow(d11_model),
              nrow(train), nrow(test),
              nrow(train_baked), nrow(test_baked)),
  Columns = c(ncol(d11_clean), ncol(d11_model),
              ncol(train), ncol(test),
              ncol(train_baked), ncol(test_baked))
)
kable(validation, caption = "Modelling preparation - before/after validation")

strat_check <- tibble(
  Set = c("Train", "Test"),
  Unemployed_Pct = c(
    round(100 * mean(train$Unemployed == 1), 2),
    round(100 * mean(test$Unemployed  == 1), 2)
  )
)
kable(strat_check, caption = "Class prevalence preserved by stratified split")

```

## 11.6 Export modelling artefacts

```{r export_model_artefacts, comment=NA}
saveRDS(train,        "data/Cleaned/train_raw.rds")
saveRDS(test,         "data/Cleaned/test_raw.rds")
saveRDS(train_baked,  "data/Cleaned/train_baked.rds")
saveRDS(test_baked,   "data/Cleaned/test_baked.rds")
saveRDS(rec_prepped,  "data/Cleaned/recipe_prepped.rds")

```

# MODELLING, EVALUATION & DEPLOYMENT

```{r setup_modelling_environment}
# 1. Read baked datasets
train_baked <- readRDS("data/Cleaned/train_baked.rds")
test_baked  <- readRDS("data/Cleaned/test_baked.rds")

# 2. Ensure Unemployed is explicitly formatted as a factor with valid level names
train_baked$Unemployed <- factor(train_baked$Unemployed, 
                                 levels = c(0, 1), 
                                 labels = c("Not_Unemployed", "Unemployed"))

test_baked$Unemployed  <- factor(test_baked$Unemployed, 
                                 levels = c(0, 1), 
                                 labels = c("Not_Unemployed", "Unemployed"))

# 3. Impute any remaining NA predictors using median imputation
impute_proc <- preProcess(train_baked, method = c("medianImpute", "zv"))
train_baked <- predict(impute_proc, train_baked)
test_baked  <- predict(impute_proc, test_baked)

```

## 1. Baseline Model — Logistic Regression

```{r model_glm}
set.seed(2026)

glm_model <- train(
  Unemployed ~ ., 
  data = train_baked, 
  method = "glm", 
  family = "binomial",
  trControl = trainControl(
    method = "cv", 
    number = 5, 
    classProbs = TRUE, 
    summaryFunction = defaultSummary
  )
)

# Predict on test set
glm_preds <- predict(glm_model, newdata = test_baked)
glm_probs <- predict(glm_model, newdata = test_baked, type = "prob")

# Performance summary
glm_cm <- confusionMatrix(
  data = glm_preds, 
  reference = test_baked$Unemployed, 
  positive = "Unemployed"
)
print(glm_cm)

```

## 2. Model — Naive Bayes

```{r model_naive_bayes}
set.seed(2026)

# Fit Naive Bayes Model using e1071
nb_model <- naiveBayes(
  Unemployed ~ ., 
  data = train_baked
)

# Predict class labels and probabilities on test set
nb_preds <- predict(nb_model, newdata = test_baked)
nb_probs <- predict(nb_model, newdata = test_baked, type = "raw")

# Performance summary via Confusion Matrix
nb_cm <- confusionMatrix(
  data = nb_preds, 
  reference = test_baked$Unemployed, 
  positive = "Unemployed"
)
print(nb_cm)

# Generate CrossTable
CrossTable(
  x = test_baked$Unemployed, 
  y = nb_preds, 
  prop.chisq = FALSE, 
  prop.c = FALSE, 
  prop.r = FALSE,
  dnn = c("Actual", "Predicted")
)

```

## 3. Advanced Model — random forest

```{r model_random_forest, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# 1. Define explicit tuning grid to bypass grid search delay
rf_grid <- expand.grid(
  mtry = floor(sqrt(ncol(train_baked) - 1)),
  splitrule = "gini",
  min.node.size = 10
)

# 2. Define train control
train_control <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 5,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary
)

set.seed(2026)

# 3. Fit ranger model across all available CPU cores
rf_model <- train(
  Unemployed ~ ., 
  data = train_baked, 
  method = "ranger", 
  trControl = train_control,
  tuneGrid = rf_grid,
  num.trees = 50,                       # Fast tree count
  num.threads = parallel::detectCores(), # Multi-threaded parallel processing
  importance = "impurity",              # Enables varImp()
  metric = "ROC"
)

# 4. Predict on test set
rf_preds <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_baked)
rf_probs <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_baked, type = "prob")

# 5. Confusion Matrix Evaluation
rf_cm <- confusionMatrix(
  data = rf_preds, 
  reference = test_baked$Unemployed, 
  positive = "Unemployed"
)
print(rf_cm)
```

## 4. Model Evaluation & ROC-AUC Comparison

```{r roc_comparison}
roc_glm <- roc(test_baked$Unemployed, glm_probs$Unemployed)
roc_nb  <- roc(test_baked$Unemployed, nb_probs[, "Unemployed"])
roc_rf  <- roc(test_baked$Unemployed, rf_probs$Unemployed)

plot(roc_glm, col = "blue", main = "ROC Curves Comparison across Models")
plot(roc_nb, col = "green", add = TRUE)
plot(roc_rf, col = "red", add = TRUE)
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = c(
         paste("GLM AUC:", round(auc(roc_glm), 3)),
         paste("NB AUC:",  round(auc(roc_nb), 3)),
         paste("C5.0 AUC:", round(auc(roc_rf), 3))
       ), 
       col = c("blue", "green", "red"), 
       lwd = 2)

```

## 5. Feature Importance Analysis

```{r feature_importance}
# Extract feature importance cleanly via caret
var_imp <- varImp(rf_model)
plot(var_imp, top = 15, main = "Top 15 Predictors of Unemployment Risk")
```
